author: miodvallat
body:
### Short description
This PR introduces a configuration flag to the LMDB backend, which, if enabled, will skip updating the domains table when the "last notified" field changes. Instead, its value will only be kept in memory as long as the domain exists and the server is running.

Other changes causing a domains table entry updated will be performed unchanged (and will write back the correct, current "last notified" value).

Of course, running in this mode will cause extra notifications to be sent upon startup, since the values read from the database will be outdated. But I've been told some lmdb users would prefer to run this way.

A forthcoming PR will implement a background task to update the domains table at a low frequency.

This PR references [the multi-agent environment commit](https://github.com/axon-rl/gem/commit/9add94a253ec28c76cebf879105eb67e6ab8d199). 

At present some flaws remain in this PR (namely it is presently not yet able to handle dictionary inputs as sequential) but that should not significantly affect its ability to **provide another perspective on how multi-agent API could look**.

### Motivation
Multi-agent environments have an additional dimension over single-agent ones in that agents either take turns, act simultaneously (or have the option to do both). 

To guide decisions along this dimension and streamline development, fundamental considerations like 
- Whether the environment features turn-taking dynamics (i.e. things that happen when relinquishing control from one agent to the next, such as dishing out cumulative rewards (present in the original commit))
- Whether the environment features global dynamics (i.e. things that only happen after ALL agents take turns, only implicitly detailed in the commit)

should be exposed to the end developer while weakly encoding some broad preferences such as simultaneous execution over sequential execution.

### Differences from [this other PR](https://github.com/axon-rl/gem/pull/79/files)
Many of the suggestions in this PR are quite similar to [the ones here](https://github.com/axon-rl/gem/pull/79/files).
The main difference is **conceptual**: 
where the two methods exist in complementary distribution in the other PR, this PR aims to **increase flexibility of this combined interface** by allowing sequential implementations to run with a simultaneous execution interface, and vice versa.

The other PR also appears to aim for an interface closer to that of [PettingZoo](https://pettingzoo.farama.org/). It is a good interface to start off of but it may be beneficial to make an interface that places the differences between sequential and simultaneous multi-agent environments front and centre (from the class definition perspective), while still maintaining convenience from the usage perspective.

author: bigspider
body:
Adds a new (alternative) `io` module that can be opted in by enabling the `io_new` feature.

The goals of the new io modules are the following:
a) Allow arbitrary size for the IO buffer, while defaulting to the usual size
b) Avoid memory waste; a single buffer used as a duplex channel is enough
c) Provide a cleaner abstraction for the duplex channel, avoiding the possibility of mistakenly using the buffer simultaneously to read from a command/apdu, or write to it for the response.

Goals (a) and (b) are fully achieved.
Goal (c) is achieved for the default usage flow as demonstrated in the boilerplate below; however, the API is not very strict so it does technically allow to make mistakes (like forgetting to respond altogether). It might be possible to come up with even stricter APIs that prevent even more misuse of the communication channel; this is left for future exploration.

In `io_new`, data is _never_ copied implicitly to or from the IO buffer. Rust ownership guarantees that the buffer is always only owned in a single place, so it can't be in 'read mode' and in 'write mode' at the same time.

In general, I think the new API is much cleaner, modular and easier to extend with future more complex features.

## Compatibility

`io` is renamed to `io_legacy`, and the new `io_new` module is part of the crate. However, they are not public modules.

If the `io_feature` is not enabled (current default), every member of `io_legacy` is exported under `io`; otherwise, `io_new` is the `io` module.

This allows to keep the new module entirely opt-in, and if the new module is considered better than the old one, migration of existing apps can happen over time.

## Breaking changes
 
As `io_new` is opt-in, there is no breaking change for existing apps. The only exception is that `Comm::new()` is no longer `const`, because that would prevent the refactoring for callbacks (see below). No app seems to be affected by this.

<del>The `init_comm` is now obsolete, as callbacks are initialized in the constructor of the `Comm` object, which should generally be a singleton. Therefore, `init_comm` is now empty (kept only to prevent a breaking change).</del>
UPDATE: partially reverted in #304 

## Feature parity

New `io_new` module should already have nearly all the features of the old module, including the BOLOS apdu handling and the `expected_cla` feature.

The only exception should be the 'automatic wait for a ticker event during apdu_send` of `io_legacy`, which is a workaround for specific apps that has a substantial performance impact in communication.

This could be reintroduced as an opt-in feature explicitly requested by apps, unless a better solution that avoids the performance impact is found.

## NBGL callbacks (refactoring)
The PR also includes a big refactoring of the NBGL integration with the `Comm<>` object, using callbacks controlled by the `Comm` object instead of embedding communication-related logic inside the Nbgl-related code.

This allows decoupling, and was essential to allow NBGL to work with either version of the `io` module.

This refactoring should be completely transparent to apps (except, it makes `init_comm` redundant).

## Case studies

The following PRs use the new io framework.
- [Boilerplate](https://github.com/LedgerHQ/app-boilerplate-rust/pull/164)
- [Vanadium](https://github.com/LedgerHQ/vanadium/pull/175)

(Vanadium is a lot more complex than the typical app in terms of communication complexity, and the PR includes substantial adaptations to take advantage of the increased IO buffer size.)

author: mcdurdin
body:
This was flagged years ago as a potential performance hotspot: each locale is loaded at process start for any kmcomapi-involved process, which takes quite a long time. This refactor moves the locale enumeration out of kmcomapi and into the build process, so we have a static list of locales put into locale/index.xml.

This includes a minor breaking change to Keyman Engine API on Windows: `MessageFromID(id, locale)` now only allows the three ids SKUILanguageName, SKUILanguageNameWithEnglish, and SKLanguageCode, for performance reasons. At this point, only SKUILanguageNameWithEnglish is actually used anywhere in Keyman, and it is unlikely that any other consumers are requesting alternate IDs.

Fixes: #14787
Build-bot: skip release:windows

# User Testing

For this test, we want to compare the startup time for Keyman Configuration with this PR vs the most recent 19.0-alpha build. This means starting Keyman Configuration multiple times.

It will be better to use the command prompt to launch Keyman Configuration for this test: `"C:\Program Files (x86)\Keyman\Keyman Desktop\kmshell.exe" -c` to avoid confusion with other UI.

The startup time is the time from pressing Enter on the command, thus starting the executable, until the Configuration window is fully displayed.

Keyman itself should not be running when you run this test.

**TEST_LANGUAGES:** Start Keyman Configuration, and verify that you can switch UI languages to the various languages that should be available, e.g. French, German, etc.

**TEST_PERFORMANCE:** Start Keyman Configuration at least 5-10 times, recording the startup time each time. and then calculate the average startup time. Do this for both the 19.0-alpha, and for this PR. The test passes if the average startup time for this PR is better than the average startup time for 19.0-alpha.

#### Problem solved by the commit
bo import export across devices 
#### Bug / issue (if any) fixed, which PR introduced the bug, how it was discovered
The bug was ZOCL was using default gem_prime_import and for that ZOCL was not freeing properly for imported BOs from other drm device drivers. 
When xdna drm device driver creates a bo and exports its handle, and ZOCL creates a bo with that handle, due to improper cleaning, the dma buf ref count was not becoming zero and it restricts to unload the xdna drm driver and memory leaks accumulate with each run.
#### How problem was solved, alternative solutions (if any) and why they were rejected
Problem was solved by adding own gem_prime_import function and keep track of the imported BOs and having a function to cleanup imported BOs.

author: edospadoni
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes large contact list loading issues that were preventing the mobile app from loading phonebooks with 20,000-25,000+ contacts.

## Changes Made

### 1. Increased PHP execution time
- Added `.user.ini` with `max_execution_time=60` to handle large contact processing
- Set `memory_limit=512M` to prevent memory exhaustion

### 2. Fixed HTTP cache headers  
- Changed `Last-Modified` header format from `DATE_RFC2822` to RFC 7231 standard (`gmdate('D, d M Y H:i:s') . ' GMT'`)
- This ensures proper HTTP caching behavior with mobile clients per Acrobits API documentation

## Problem Solved

Before: Large contact lists (20k+ contacts) would timeout and fail to load in the mobile app
After: Contact lists load successfully within the 60-second timeout limit with proper caching

## Testing

- Tested with 28,426 contacts - loads successfully 
- HTTP cache headers now properly trigger 304 Not Modified responses
- Memory usage stays stable around 80-120MB during processing

## Future Considerations

A streaming mechanism could be implemented if the mobile app supports it, to avoid processing all contacts at once. However, this optimization is not critical since very few phonebooks are this large - most contain 150-500 contacts.

To ease the process of reviewing your PR, do make sure to complete the following boxes.

## Type of Changes

<!-- Leave the corresponding lines for the applicable type of change: -->

|     | Type                   |
| --- | ---------------------- |
|    | :bug: Bug fix          |
| ✓   | :sparkles: New feature |
|    | :hammer: Refactoring   |
|    | :scroll: Docs          |

## Description

<!-- If this PR references an issue without fixing it: -->

This PR builds on #1189 by implementing the constraint interface to handle boolean constraints, similar to how `None` constraints are currently treated.

Previously, constraints only accounted for `None` checks:
```
x = 1

if x is None:
    x    # Uninferable, `1` is filtered out because x is not None
```

These changes support constraints derived from boolean truthiness:

1. If condition is `True`, keep the inferred value.
```
x = 1    # truthy

if x:
    x    # inferred as `1`
```

2. If condition is `False`, filter out the inferred value.
```
x = []    # falsy

if x:
    x    # Uninferable, `[]` filtered out
```

3. Negation rules are the same as `None` constraints.
```
x = 1

if x:
    pass
else:
    x    # Uninferable, `1` filtered out


y = []

if not y:
    y    # inferred as `[]`
```

4. If the boolean value cannot be inferred, assume constraint is satisfied.


Closes https://github.com/pylint-dev/pylint/issues/9515

This PR adds comprehensive support for Vertex AI dedicated endpoints in LiteLLM, enabling users to leverage dedicated endpoint URL patterns like `https://${ENDPOINT_ID}.us-central1-222900905574.prediction.vertexai.goog/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/locations/us-central1/endpoints/${ENDPOINT_ID}:predict`.

### Key Features Added

1. **Dedicated Endpoint Detection**: Automatically detects dedicated endpoints based on `mg-endpoint-` pattern in `model_id` parameter
2. **Sync Completion Support**: Full support for synchronous completion using `aiplatform.Endpoint` class
3. **Async Completion Support**: Async completion with graceful fallback to synchronous predict
4. **Async Streaming Support**: Async streaming using `TextStreamer` for fake streaming experience
5. **Automatic URL Construction**: Leverages Google Cloud SDK's built-in dedicated endpoint URL construction

### Implementation Details

#### Detection Logic
```python
elif model == "dedicated" or (optional_params.get("model_id") and "mg-endpoint-" in optional_params.get("model_id", "")):
    mode = "dedicated"
    model = optional_params.pop("model_id", model)
    # ... dedicated endpoint handling
```

#### Basic Usage
```python
response = litellm.completion(
    model="vertex_ai/any-model-name",  # Gets ignored
    messages=[{"content": "Hello!"}],
    model_id="mg-endpoint-your-endpoint-id",  # Triggers dedicated mode
    vertex_project="your-project",
    vertex_location="us-central1"
)
```

author: copilot
body:
This PR extends the external-secrets-configuration helm chart by adding support for the `decodingStrategy` parameter, enabling automatic decoding of base64-encoded secrets as documented in the External Secrets decoding strategy guide.

## What's Changed

The chart now supports automatic base64 decoding through the `decodingStrategy` parameter at both global and individual secret levels:

```yaml
# Global configuration - applies to all secrets
decodingStrategy: "Auto"

objects:
  database-secrets:
    data:
      - secretKey: username
        remoteRef: db-username
        # Uses global "Auto" strategy
      - secretKey: password
        remoteRef: db-password
        decodingStrategy: "Base64"  # Override global setting
  
  json-config:
    dataFrom:
      - remoteRef: app-config-json
        decodingStrategy: "Auto"  # Per-dataFrom override
```

## Key Features

- **Global Configuration**: Set `decodingStrategy` once to apply to all secrets
- **Per-Secret Override**: Individual `data` entries can specify their own strategy
- **DataFrom Support**: JSON secrets via `dataFrom` also support decoding strategies
- **Multiple Strategies**: Supports `"Auto"`, `"Base64"`, `"None"`, or omitted values
- **Backward Compatibility**: Existing configurations continue to work unchanged

## Available Decoding Strategies

- `"Auto"` - Automatically detect and decode base64-encoded content
- `"Base64"` - Force base64 decoding regardless of content
- `"None"` - Explicitly disable decoding
- Empty/omitted - Uses External Secrets operator default behavior

## Version Update

Chart version bumped from `0.0.7` to `0.0.8` as a minor release, maintaining semantic versioning for this backward-compatible feature addition.

## Testing

All changes have been validated with:
- Helm lint passes without errors
- Template generation tested with various configuration scenarios
- Backward compatibility verified with existing configurations
- Generated YAML conforms to External Secrets API specification

The implementation follows External Secrets operator best practices and enables flexible secret decoding workflows while maintaining the chart's simplified configuration approach.

body: Closes #1661 #### Problem Users who previously stored network states using the Python spike queue fallback (before Cython spike queue became mandatory) cannot restore these files with current Brian2 versions. This creates a backwards compatibility regression where valid saved states become unusable. **Error when loading Python spike queue states:** ``` ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2) ``` **Root cause:** The two spike queue implementations use different internal state formats: - **Python format:** `(time, spike_array, dimensions)` - stores relationships as `[delay_bin, synapse_index]` pairs - **Cython format:** `(offset, spike_lists)` - stores spike lists per delay slot in circular buffer Fixed now : cc : @mstimberg

author: overlookmotel
body:
Add visitor keys export to `oxc-parser` NPM package. This is useful in itself, but also the first step towards an ESTree walker.

Visitor keys are based on `@typescript-eslint/visitor-keys`.

It'd be ideal to generate visitor keys direct from Oxc's own types, but that's proving difficult due to all the custom serializers we use to translate to ESTree. So using the shortcut of borrowing from TS-ESLint for now.

Oxc's AST is slightly different from TS-ESTree (notably Oxc's AST adds `ParenthesizedExpression`). But apart from those few differences, TS-ESLint's AST and Oxc's are identical, and I made a PR to TS-ESLint earlier this year (https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/pull/11279) to ensure visitor key order is correct, and matches Oxc.

To avoid adding a runtime dependency on `@typescript-eslint/visitor-keys`, extract the data from TS-ESLint in `oxc_ast_tools`, amend for Oxc/TS-ESTree differences, and re-output it as a simple object literal.

This approach will be faster at runtime, as the object's shape is consistent, and also avoids a dependency.

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

When creating users through the admin interface (`/admin/users`) with invalid form data, the application was returning a 500 Internal Server Error instead of displaying helpful validation error messages. This occurred due to a `NoMethodError` in the form error handling code.

The specific error was:
```
NoMethodError (undefined method '+' for nil):
config/initializers/action_view_fields_with_errors.rb:8:in 'block in <main>'
```

This happened when form fields didn't have an existing `class` attribute, causing `element["class"]` to return `nil`, and the code attempted to concatenate a string to `nil` using the `+` operator.

## Solution

Fixed the `field_error_proc` in `config/initializers/action_view_fields_with_errors.rb` to safely handle nil class attributes:

**Before (buggy code):**
```ruby
if element && %w[input].include?(element.name)
  element["class"] += " is-invalid"  # ❌ NoMethodError when class is nil
  fragment.to_html.html_safe
```

**After (fixed code):**
```ruby
if element && %w[input].include?(element.name)
  existing_class = element["class"] || ""
  element["class"] = existing_class.empty? ? "is-invalid" : "#{existing_class} is-invalid"
  fragment.to_html.html_safe
```

## Testing

Added comprehensive tests to ensure the fix works correctly:

1. **Unit tests** for the field error proc covering:
   - Form fields with no class attribute
   - Form fields with empty class attribute  
   - Form fields with existing class attributes
   - Non-input elements (should remain unchanged)

2. **Integration tests** for admin user creation scenarios:
   - Valid user creation (should succeed)
   - Invalid password length (should show validation errors, not 500)
   - Invalid email format (should show validation errors, not 500)
   - Duplicate email addresses (should show validation errors, not 500)

## Impact

- ✅ Admin users now see proper validation error messages instead of 500 errors
- ✅ Form fields are properly highlighted with `is-invalid` CSS class on validation errors
- ✅ Better user experience for admin user management
- ✅ No breaking changes to existing functionality

This fix resolves the core issue where validation failures in the admin interface caused server crashes instead of displaying user-friendly error messages.

Fixes #3700.

# Summary | Résumé

Our release-please workflow pushes a commit to the release PR that updates the tag that's deployed to `test`. This is working, but [actions performed by the default GITHUB_TOKEN do not kick off CI](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow#triggering-a-workflow-from-a-workflow). So CI is not running on our [release PR](https://github.com/cds-snc/gc-signin-user-selfservice-webapp/pull/708) right now.

This change uses the same token that we're using to push the initial PR to also push the change to `.deployed_versions/test`.

author: pauldambra
body:
we let users find session recordings by event property

e.g. show me recordings for url X or where flag Y was control

this doesn't recruit the `order by` of the events table and we end up reading lots of rows

we _should_ read fewer rows if we look up the events that the property is on and then pass them into the query instead

so instead of `show me recordings for url X` which translates to `find any event where property url is X and get its session ids` we'd instead translate to `find _these_ events where...` 

we already see a case where a user can't run a query because it timesout e.g. https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/38197 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/40673) where this should help

---

This PR

* adds a feature flag to control the new behaviour
* uses that to alter API parameter to enable or not the new behaviour
* and adds a mode (controller by the flag) to the event subquery in replay that can load all event names for a property and include that in the query

this should let ClickHouse skip _way_ more data and not timeout
in the case in the linked zendesk ticket we were reading billions of rows mostly unnecessarily

author: reynoldsbd
body:
### Pull Request Overview

This PR enables the use of Virtio devices on the x86 architecture.

A new library, _chips/pci/_, provides lower-level facilities for interacting with PCI devices. It adheres closely to the PCI Local Bus specification, version 3, as published by PCI-SIG.

The existing _chips/virtio/_ library is expanded with an additional transport driver for PCI, using the above-mentioned library to interact with devices. This transport driver is a drop-in replacement for the existing MMIO-based transport; no code changes are needed in any of the shared Virtio code in order for a device to work on the new backend.

The QEMU Q35 emulated board is updated to enumerate and initialize a Virtio RNG device during kernel startup. This serves as an illustration not only of iterating and detecting Virtio PCI devices, but also of handling arbitrary PCI interrupts on the x86 platform using a custom `InterruptService` implementation.


### Testing Strategy

Ran `make run` on qemu_i486_q35 board, confirmed it continues to build and run cleanly with the added virtio driver.

Ran Pluton's internal RNG test suite against Virtio RNG driver.


### TODO or Help Wanted

The Pluton environment is somewhat different from upstream. I don't believe these differences are substantive with respect to testing integration of a Virtio RNG device. Nevertheless, having some other party validate the functionality of the Virtio RNG device on the upstream QEMU Q35 board would provide greater confidence in the correctness of this feature.

author: cristianglezm
body:
This commit introduces a major architectural change to decouple the computationally expensive flower genetics calculations from the main simulation loop, ensuring a consistent and non-blocking tick rate.

1.  **Dual-Worker Architecture:**
    *   **`simulation.worker.ts` (Simulation Host):** This worker's sole responsibility is to own the simulation state and run the main game loop (`calculateNextTick`). It is never blocked by slow operations.
    *   **`flower.worker.ts` (Genetics Worker):** A new, dedicated worker that owns the WASM module (`FEService`). Its only job is to handle expensive, asynchronous requests for creating, mutating, and reproducing flowers.

2.  **Asynchronous Flower Creation Pipeline:**
    *   When the simulation engine needs a new flower, it no longer calls the WASM service directly and waits.
    *   Instead, it immediately places a lightweight `FlowerSeed` placeholder actor on the grid.
    *   It sends an asynchronous message to the `flower.worker.ts` to generate the full flower data in the background.
    *   Once the Genetics Worker completes its task, it sends the full `Flower` data back to the Simulation Host.
    *   At the start of the next tick, the engine seamlessly replaces the `FlowerSeed` with the fully-formed `Flower`.

3.  **Refactored Initialization:**
    *   The creation of the initial set of actors is now fully managed within the `simulation.worker.ts`, which asynchronously requests the initial flowers from the `flower.worker.ts`. This removes heavy setup logic from the main thread.

4.  **UI & State Management:**
    *   The `useSimulation` hook now manages the lifecycle of both workers and establishes a `MessageChannel` for their communication.
    *   The rendering engine has been updated to draw `FlowerSeed` placeholders.
    *   Error handling has been added to `App.tsx` to catch critical worker failures.

This new architecture ensures the UI remains perfectly responsive and the simulation progresses at a steady pace, even when multiple complex flowers are being generated simultaneously.

author: pvillard31
body:
# Summary

NIFI-14995 - Improve Flow Differences Filter to account for renameProperty and createControllerService

As we use more and more the `migrateProperties` capabilities, we see that we have some corner cases where the automated changes are showing as local changes which is confusing because a user is upgrading without making any changes to their versioned flows and the UI is showing that some local modifications have been made. Such scenarios should be better handled to not show local changes.

One scenario has been handled in [NIFI-14985](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/NIFI-14985) to better deal with removed properties.

This change is to handle two additional scenarios (this is combined in a single PR because of the approach taken that is introducing a concept of environmental context)

### Rename property with parameters

Let's consider a processor version N with

````java
    public static final PropertyDescriptor ACCESS_KEY_ID = new PropertyDescriptor.Builder()
        .name("Access Key")
        .displayName("Access Key ID")
        .expressionLanguageSupported(ExpressionLanguageScope.ENVIRONMENT)
        .required(false)
        .addValidator(StandardValidators.NON_EMPTY_VALIDATOR)
        .sensitive(true)
        .build();
````

And then version N+1 with

````java
    public static final PropertyDescriptor ACCESS_KEY_ID = new PropertyDescriptor.Builder()
        .name("Access Key ID")
        .expressionLanguageSupported(ExpressionLanguageScope.ENVIRONMENT)
        .required(false)
        .addValidator(StandardValidators.NON_EMPTY_VALIDATOR)
        .sensitive(true)
        .build();
...
    public void migrateProperties(PropertyConfiguration config) {
        config.renameProperty("Access Key", ACCESS_KEY_ID.getName());
    }
````

If the versioned flow is containing:

````json
       "groupIdentifier" : "flow-contents-group",
       "identifier" : "8de3b31b-0a70-3e01-a01c-4ed2fe3a4cbe",
       "name" : "AWS Credentials Provider",
       "properties" : {
         "Access Key" : "#{AWS Access Key ID}",
         "default-credentials" : "false",
         "Session Time" : "3600",
         "assume-role-sts-signer-override" : "Default Signature",
         "assume-role-sts-region" : "us-west-2",
         "Secret Key" : "#{AWS Secret Access Key}",
         "anonymous-credentials" : "false"
       }, 
````

Then we would show two local changes:
- Property Parameterization Removed - Property 'Access Key ID' is no longer a parameter reference
- Property Parameterized - Property 'Access Key ID' was parameterized

We should not be showing this as local changes.

### Create Controller Service

When using something like:

````java
     @Override
     public void migrateProperties(final PropertyConfiguration config) {
         if (!config.isPropertySet(ABC.getName())) {
             final String serviceId = config.createControllerService(
                     "org.apache.nifi.foo",
                     Map.of());
             config.setProperty(ABC, serviceId);
         }
         super.migrateProperties(config);
     } 
````

Then we would be showing two local changes:
- Property Added: the property ABC has been added
- Component Created: a controller service has been created

We should check that if the property being added is not a dynamic property, and is referencing the UUID of the created controller service, then both changes should not be showing as local changes.

### Approach

Introducing a richer `EnvironmentalChangeContext` that is reused across all comparisons. This is how we can link a couple of differences as related to the same change and decide to filter out the differences or not.

author: chalmerlowe
body:
The `_AsyncJob.result()` method was not correctly passing the right arguments to the superclass's `result()` method when the `retry` object was expected to be the same as the `DEFAULT_RETRY` object. Passing an empty `dict` was a way of simply letting the `google.api_core` handle things. 

```
{} if retry is DEFAULT_RETRY else {"retry": retry}
```

When the `retry` object is instantiated and when the `DEFAULT_RETRY` object is instantiated, these two elements are separate objects. This means that because the `is` keyword checks for **identity** NOT **equality** that code path never evaluates to `True` and is not used as one would expect.  

This leads to subtle bugs that this PR corrects by simply passing the `retry` object and relying on the `google.api_core` to understand what a `DEFAULT_RETRY` value is and managing it appropriately.

A new test case is added to verify that `job.result()` correctly handles both the default retry use case and a custom retry object use case.

Fixes #2210 🦕

author: copilot
body:
This PR introduces a comprehensive Python package (`mibi_analysis/`) that extracts and modularizes the key functionality from `notebooks/multicellular/MOFACell.ipynb` into reusable helper functions for preprocessing, running MuVI factor analysis, and visualizing results. The package follows the exact patterns, dependencies, and workflows from MOFACell.ipynb.

## New Package Structure

The package provides four main modules:

### `mibi_analysis.preprocessing`
- `normalize_mudata_features()`: Center and scale features across modalities (extracted from MOFACell.ipynb)
- `prepare_mudata_for_mofa()`: Complete preprocessing pipeline for factor analysis
- `get_modality_stats()`: Generate summary statistics for data quality assessment

### `mibi_analysis.mofa`
- `get_device()`: GPU/CPU device detection using `muvi.get_free_gpu_idx()` (as in MOFACell.ipynb)
- `run_mofa_analysis()`: Convenient wrapper for `mu.tl.mofa` with same parameters as MOFACell.ipynb
- `calculate_model_r2()`: Compute model variance explained metrics
- `extract_factor_scores()`: Extract factor scores using liana utilities (`li.ut.get_factor_scores()`) as preferred method
- `extract_factor_loadings()`: Get factor loadings using liana utilities (`li.ut.get_variable_loadings()`) as preferred method

### `mibi_analysis.visualization`
- `get_cov_ellipse()`: Generate confidence ellipse points (directly extracted from MOFACell.ipynb)
- `plot_factor_scores()`: Factor score scatter plots with optional confidence ellipses using plotnine
- `plot_factor_loadings()`: Heatmap visualizations of factor loadings
- `plot_r2_explained()`: Variance explained bar plots by modality

### `mibi_analysis.interpretation`
- `test_factor_associations()`: Statistical testing of factor-clinical associations using Kruskal-Wallis (as in MOFACell.ipynb)
- `identify_top_loadings()`: Find most important features per factor
- `summarize_factor_by_group()`: Generate group-wise summary statistics
- `calculate_factor_stability()`: Assess factor stability through bootstrap resampling

## Dependencies Following MOFACell.ipynb

The package now properly relies on the same dependencies as MOFACell.ipynb:
- **muon**: For MuData operations and MOFA analysis via `mu.tl.mofa`
- **muvi**: For GPU device detection and MuVI-specific functionality
- **liana**: For factor score and loading extraction utilities (`li.ut.get_factor_scores()`, `li.ut.get_variable_loadings()`)
- **plotnine**: For visualization with `from plotnine import *` pattern

## Usage Example Following MOFACell.ipynb Patterns

```python
import mibi_analysis as ma
import muon as mu
import liana as li
from plotnine import *

# Device detection (MOFACell.ipynb pattern)
device = ma.get_device()

# Load data (MOFACell.ipynb variable naming)
features = mu.read_h5mu("data/celltype_features_with_functional_markers.h5mu")

# Preprocess (same normalization as MOFACell.ipynb)
ma.prepare_mudata_for_mofa(features, normalize=True, filter_features=True)

# Run MOFA analysis (same parameters as MOFACell.ipynb)
model_path = ma.run_mofa_analysis(
    features, 
    n_factors=10,
    use_obs='union',
    convergence_mode='medium',
    scale_groups=False,
    scale_views=False,
    seed=1337
)

# Extract using liana utilities (MOFACell.ipynb approach)
factor_scores = ma.extract_factor_scores(
    features, 
    obsm_key='X_mofa', 
    obs_keys=['Stage'],
    use_liana=True  # Uses li.ut.get_factor_scores()
)

variable_loadings = ma.extract_factor_loadings(
    features,
    varm_key='LFs',
    use_liana=True  # Uses li.ut.get_variable_loadings()
)

# Test associations using Kruskal-Wallis (as in MOFACell.ipynb)
associations = ma.test_factor_associations(
    factor_scores, 
    clinical_variables=['Stage', 'Sex'],
    test_type='kruskal',
    correction_method='bonferroni'
)

# Visualize with confidence ellipses (as in MOFACell.ipynb)
plot = ma.plot_factor_scores(
    factor_scores, 
    'Factor1', 'Factor2',  # Note: liana uses 'Factor1' not 'Factor 1'
    color_by='Stage', 
    add_ellipses=True,
    title='Factor Analysis Results'
)
```

## Package Installation

The package can be installed in development mode:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

## Documentation and Examples

- Complete package documentation in `mibi_analysis/README.md`
- Example workflow in `examples/mibi_analysis_example.ipynb` following MOFACell.ipynb patterns
- Updated main README with package information and usage instructions
- Comprehensive docstrings with examples for all functions

## Key Benefits

1. **MOFACell.ipynb Compatibility**: Functions follow the exact same patterns, imports, and workflows as the original notebook
2. **Modular Design**: Separates preprocessing, analysis, visualization, and interpretation into focused modules
3. **Reusability**: Functions can be used across different MIBI analysis workflows
4. **Backward Compatibility**: Original function signatures still supported with fallback mechanisms
5. **Proper Dependencies**: Now relies on muon, muvi, liana, and plotnine as required
6. **Documentation**: Well-documented API with examples and type hints
7. **Testing Ready**: Package structure supports easy addition of unit tests

This package transforms the notebook-based analysis into a production-ready tool while preserving all the statistical rigor and visualization capabilities of the original MOFACell.ipynb workflow, with functions that mirror the exact same approach users would follow in the notebook.

### Added Clippy Restrictions
Added three new clippy warning rules to the root `Cargo.toml`:
- `panic_in_result_fn = "warn"` - Prevents panics in functions that return `Result`
- `todo = "warn"` - Flags TODO comments for review
- `unwrap_used = "warn"` - Highlights potential panic points from unwrap calls

### Fixed Production Code Issue
The new `panic_in_result_fn` lint identified an issue in `martin/src/config/file/pmtiles.rs` where the `init_parsing` method was using `assert!()` in a function that returns `ConfigFileResult<()>`. This could cause unexpected panics instead of proper error handling.

**Before:**
```rust
fn init_parsing(&mut self, cache: OptMainCache) -> ConfigFileResult<()> {
    assert!(
        self.cache.is_none(),
        "init_parsing should only be called once"
    );
    // ...
}
```

**After:**
```rust
fn init_parsing(&mut self, cache: OptMainCache) -> ConfigFileResult<()> {
    if self.cache.is_some() {
        return Err(ConfigFileError::ConfigInitializationAlreadyCalled);
    }
    // ...
}
```

Added a new `ConfigInitializationAlreadyCalled` error variant to `ConfigFileError` to properly handle this case.

## Impact

- **Production code is now panic-free** in result-returning functions
- **Better error handling** - callers can now properly handle initialization errors instead of experiencing unexpected panics
- **Improved code quality** through stricter linting rules
- **Remaining warnings** are confined to test code where panics via `assert!()` are acceptable

The clippy check now passes for production code, with only test-related warnings remaining (which is expected and acceptable).

Fixes #2204.

author: dterrahe
body:
An incorrect fix for shortcuts to utility module presets not working (#19075) causes many strings to be untranslated in the shortcuts dialog and other assorted breakage. AgX used a "modified" pattern for section names (using C_ instead of NC_) presumably to work around this breakage.

I realise it is hard to test if a change in a crucial section of shortcut handling possibly causes problems in any area that you are not currently working on, but it is probably safe to assume that it will. However, not everybody would understand all the different areas that could be impacted and therefore need to be tested. We don't have any automated test scripts for user interface interactions/display and I don't see how we could have them without building a whole testing framework first. Besides, translations are a confusing subject and breakage can be unnoticeable to English users/developers.

So I've spent some time writing down how translations are dealt with and a manual test script that should be run through to catch regressions, basically at least whenever `accelerators.c` or any of `dt_util_localize_` is touched. I've put it here https://github.com/dterrahe/darktable/wiki/document-translation-marking-for-developers and hope that some form of it would be acceptable in the developers wiki. Maybe the test script should be moved somewhere separate. I have no suggestions where though. Feedback very much appreciated.

It could be interesting to walk through the test script on master and see how much breakage users are apparently used to ignoring without feeling an urge to report it.

author: abhinav92003
body:
Enables PC continuity checks in the invariant_checker that verify control flow continuity of the branch_target marker value to the post-syscall trace pc.

Until #7639, the syscall-trace-end branch_target marker always held the syscall-fallthrough pc, but now it holds the pc of the actual next instr in the thread. This solves two previously-unhandled cases: auto-restart syscalls that resume control at the syscall pc itself, and control-transferring syscalls like sigreturn that resume control at some arbitrary pc.

Also manually ran the invariant checker on two large internal app traces (x86 and aarch64), and confirmed that no unexpected invariant errors were reported.

Issue: #7496

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

In the hierarchical Bayesian group-level model (`hmetad_groupLevel`), the key parameters `d1`, `meta_d`, `c1`, and `c2` were computed during model fitting but not stored as PyMC variables, making them unavailable in the resulting `idata` posterior samples. Users could only access hierarchical parameters like `Mratio` but not the group-level statistics of primary interest.

## Solution

Updated `metadpy/models/group_level_pymc.py` to store group-level statistics as PyMC `Deterministic` variables:

- **`d1_group_mean`, `d1_group_std`**: Group-level mean and standard deviation of Type 1 d-prime across subjects
- **`c1_group_mean`, `c1_group_std`**: Group-level mean and standard deviation of Type 1 criterion across subjects
- **`meta_d_group_mean`, `meta_d_group_std`**: Group-level mean and standard deviation of meta-d-prime across subjects
- **`c2_group_mean`, `c2_group_std`**: Group-level mean and standard deviation of Type 2 confidence criteria across subjects

The implementation was applied to the vectorized hierarchical model structure from the master branch, ensuring compatibility with the latest performance improvements while adding the requested group-level parameter access.

## Example Usage

```python
from metadpy.bayesian import hmetad
from metadpy import load_dataset

# Load group data
group_df = load_dataset('rm')

# Fit hierarchical model
model, traces = hmetad(
    data=group_df,
    stimuli='Stimuli',
    accuracy='Accuracy',
    confidence='Confidence',
    subject='Subject',
    nRatings=4
)

# Access group-level statistics from idata
d1_mean_samples = traces.posterior['d1_group_mean']  # Shape: (chains, draws)

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The Bitcoin Mining News Bot was failing to post threaded tweets due to an incorrect Twitter API parameter. While the first tweet in each thread was posting successfully, the reply tweet was failing with this error:

```
Client.create_tweet() got an unexpected keyword argument 'reply'
```

This prevented the bot from posting complete tweet threads with article links, reducing the effectiveness of the automated posting system.

## Root Cause

The bot was using an outdated API parameter format for creating reply tweets:

```python
# Incorrect - causing the error
reply_parameters = {"in_reply_to_tweet_id": first_tweet_id}
second_tweet = self.twitter_client.create_tweet(
    text=f"Read more: {article_url}",
    reply=reply_parameters  # ❌ Invalid parameter
)
```

The Twitter API v2 (via Tweepy 4.x) expects the `in_reply_to_tweet_id` parameter to be passed directly, not nested in a `reply` object.

## Solution

Updated the API call to use the correct parameter format:

```python
# Correct - matches Twitter API v2 specification
second_tweet = self.twitter_client.create_tweet(
    text=f"Read more: {article_url}",
    in_reply_to_tweet_id=first_tweet_id  # ✅ Valid parameter
)
```

## Changes Made

- **bot.py**: Fixed the Twitter API call for creating reply tweets
- **test_success_scenario.py**: Updated test assertions to match the correct API usage
- **tests/test_fetch_articles.py**: Fixed test expectations for the threading functionality

## Testing

All tests now pass (8/8), including specific tests that verify:
- Reply tweets are created with the correct `in_reply_to_tweet_id` parameter
- Complete tweet threads are posted successfully
- The bot handles articles with and without URLs correctly

## Impact

This fix ensures that the bot will post complete tweet threads instead of just single tweets, providing users with proper article links and improving the overall functionality of the automated Bitcoin mining news service.

body:
This PR implements automated LinkedIn job search scheduling functionality by integrating the existing LinkedIn CrewAI crew with the scheduler and queue infrastructure.

## Overview

The implementation adds LinkedIn-specific routing to the existing job scheduling system, allowing LinkedIn site schedules to automatically trigger LinkedIn CrewAI searches instead of regular web scraping.

## Key Changes

### Worker Function (`app/services/infrastructure/worker.py`)
- Added `run_linkedin_job_search()` worker function that integrates with the existing LinkedIn CrewAI crew
- Converts LinkedIn search results to jobspy format for seamless database persistence
- Includes comprehensive error handling and run status tracking

### Queue Service Extension (`app/services/infrastructure/queue.py`)
- Added `enqueue_linkedin_job_search()` method to handle LinkedIn-specific job queuing
- Uses existing RQ queue infrastructure with LinkedIn-specific run ID prefixes
- Maintains compatibility with existing queue patterns

### Scheduler Service Update (`app/services/infrastructure/scheduler.py`)
- Modified `process_scheduled_sites()` to detect LinkedIn sites (`site_name = "linkedin"`)
- Routes LinkedIn sites to LinkedIn search queue while preserving regular scraping for other sites
- No changes to existing scheduling logic or database tracking

### Docker Configuration (`docker-compose.yml`)
- Added LinkedIn credentials to worker container environment variables
- Added MCP Gateway dependency for LinkedIn MCP server access
- Ensures workers have access to `LINKEDIN_EMAIL`, `LINKEDIN_PASSWORD`, and `LINKEDIN_COOKIE`

## How It Works

1. **Scheduler Detection**: The scheduler identifies enabled LinkedIn site schedules from the database
2. **Smart Routing**: LinkedIn sites are routed to `enqueue_linkedin_job_search()` while other sites use regular scraping
3. **CrewAI Integration**: The worker executes the existing LinkedIn CrewAI crew with transformed parameters
4. **Job Persistence**: LinkedIn search results are converted to jobspy format and persisted to the database
5. **Status Tracking**: All operations are tracked in the `scrape_runs` table with detailed logging

## Database Integration

The existing database schema already includes a LinkedIn site schedule (disabled by default). To activate:

```sql
UPDATE site_schedules SET enabled = true WHERE site_name = 'linkedin';
```

LinkedIn jobs are automatically persisted to the existing `jobs` table with `site = 'linkedin'` and deduplicated against existing records.

## Backwards Compatibility

This implementation maintains full backwards compatibility:
- Existing job scraping functionality is unchanged
- No modifications to existing API endpoints
- Database schema remains intact
- All existing site schedules continue to work as before

The changes are surgical and focused, adding LinkedIn scheduling capability without disrupting any existing functionality.

Fixes #236.

1. Add 10 total attempts forn CFAM read/write/writeWithMask before considering it a failure.
2. Add the same number of attempts when checking if if the sibling CFAM device is present.
3. Put the sibling CFAM device presence on D-Bus using the Availability interface.

When an FSI scan runs it destroys and recreates all CFAMs, so these commits protect against that being seen as a hard failure.

The new Available property will be used on systems that don't have sibling presence GPIOs to know if there is another BMC present.

author: copilot
body:
This PR resolves the issue where AgentSight fails to capture SSL/TLS traffic from Node.js applications installed via NVM (Node Version Manager). The problem occurs because NVM-distributed Node.js binaries statically link OpenSSL libraries instead of using system shared libraries that AgentSight's UProbes normally attach to.

## Problem

```bash
# This works - system Node.js uses shared libssl.so
sudo ./agentsight record -c "node"  # ✅ Captures SSL traffic

# This fails - NVM Node.js has statically-linked SSL
~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.0.0/bin/node claude-cli  # ❌ No SSL traffic captured
```

The issue affects popular AI tools like Claude CLI and Gemini CLI that run on NVM-installed Node.js.

## Solution

Added a new `--binary-path` command-line option that allows AgentSight to attach UProbes directly to executable binaries with statically-linked SSL libraries:

```bash
# Monitor NVM Node.js applications
sudo ./agentsight ssl --binary-path ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.0.0/bin/node --comm node

# Quick record command for NVM binaries  
sudo ./agentsight record -c node -- --binary-path ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20.0.0/bin/node
```

## Implementation Details

- **eBPF Enhancement**: Extended `sslsniff.c` to accept `--binary-path` parameter using existing `EXTRA_LIB_KEY` infrastructure
- **Binary Attachment**: Added logic to attach OpenSSL UProbes directly to specified executable in addition to system libraries
- **Rust Integration**: Leveraged existing argument passthrough mechanism (`-- <ARGS>...`) for seamless collector integration
- **Memory Management**: Proper cleanup for dynamically allocated strings
- **Backward Compatibility**: All existing functionality preserved

## Testing

Verified with real Node.js binary (`/usr/local/bin/node`):
- ✅ Successfully resolves SSL symbols: `SSL_write`, `SSL_read`, `SSL_write_ex`, `SSL_read_ex`, `SSL_do_handshake`
- ✅ Monitors both system libraries and custom binaries simultaneously
- ✅ All existing tests continue to pass
- ✅ Rust collector integration working via argument passthrough

## Documentation

Updated README with:
- **Comprehensive NVM Section**: Added detailed "Problem" section and "Root Cause Analysis" explaining the technical difference between system-packaged Node.js (dynamic linking) and NVM Node.js (static linking)
- **Enhanced FAQ**: Expanded FAQ entry with technical explanation comparing dynamic vs static linking approaches
- **Usage Examples**: Complete command reference with binary-path examples

body:
crop_scaleの実装をモジュール化します。

## 要約（自動生成）

This pull request refactors the crop and scale command implementation to improve maintainability and extensibility. The main changes include extracting FFmpeg crop/scale logic into a new `CropScaler` class, introducing a flexible progress reporting system, and cleaning up legacy code. Additionally, it adds a submodule for test fixtures. Below are the most important changes:

**Refactoring and Code Organization**
* Moved the FFmpeg crop and scale logic from `aoirint_matvtool/crop_scale.py` into a new class `CropScaler` in `aoirint_matvtool/video_utility/crop_scaler.py`, encapsulating related functionality and improving separation of concerns. The original procedural implementation was removed. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-de06901d2858fc56071c36d9b1f6c20e003914ddfc132d4dd044a0b1c8249a9dR1-R108) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aac7f16380b71cf1a6f81178a43164298713d71af927cf8d79163bf707981b52L1-L114)

**Progress Reporting System**
* Introduced a new progress handler interface (`ProgressHandler`) in `aoirint_matvtool/progress_handler/base.py` and two implementations: plain text (`ProgressHandlerPlain`) and tqdm-based (`ProgressHandlerTqdm`). This allows flexible reporting of FFmpeg progress during crop/scale operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7f41310b11d784be07738cc495f62585df38cc5b0834d49a0c28f97f651b6926R1-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6cce6b47b1e4688b899bcdf42f82d30f3ccd453fcf144acdf22298ac6c56c91dR1-R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-eac752bd88738dd6cf844230871eba5d4a985233fd7355b93392e6562eca6478R1-R41)
* Updated `aoirint_matvtool/command/crop_scale.py` to use the new progress handler system, passing progress updates from `CropScaler` to the appropriate handler based on CLI options. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-52bc75ca98a0c1d1d1636017ece055e0d16fbb03f572d38f4d61ed4bc0662cefL1-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-52bc75ca98a0c1d1d1636017ece055e0d16fbb03f572d38f4d61ed4bc0662cefR25-L60) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-52bc75ca98a0c1d1d1636017ece055e0d16fbb03f572d38f4d61ed4bc0662cefR63-R64) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-52bc75ca98a0c1d1d1636017ece055e0d16fbb03f572d38f4d61ed4bc0662cefR79-R80)

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete **Visual Analysis Agent** system based on the specifications in `agent.md`. The agent performs comprehensive image analysis through a structured 5-step workflow and generates progressive prompts for text-to-image generation models.

## Implementation Overview

The system transforms images into detailed, structured textual descriptions that can be used to reconstruct the original image's essence, style, and mood through AI image generation.

### Core Features

**5-Step Analysis Workflow:**
1. **Initial Ingestion & High-Level Triage** - Extracts metadata, categorizes images, assesses mood
2. **Compositional & Structural Analysis** - Analyzes layout rules, focal points, depth layers
3. **Shape & Form Deconstruction** - Breaks down objects into geometric and organic shapes
4. **Color Palette & Lighting Analysis** - Identifies dominant colors, lighting sources and quality
5. **Texture & Material Definition** - Analyzes surface textures and material properties

**Progressive Prompt Generation:**
- **Level 1:** Core concept with essential elements
- **Level 2:** Adds compositional structure and layout
- **Level 3:** Incorporates artistic mood, lighting, and colors
- **Level 4:** Complete technical blueprint with textures and shapes

### Usage Examples

**Python API:**
```python
from visual_analysis_agent import VisualAnalysisAgent

agent = VisualAnalysisAgent()
results = agent.analyze_image('landscape.jpg')

# Access individual analysis steps
print(results['step1'].output)  # Initial triage
print(results['step4'].output)  # Color and lighting

# Get progressive prompts
prompts = results['prompts']
print(prompts['level4'])  # Master blueprint prompt
```

**Command Line Interface:**
```bash
# Full analysis
python cli.py image.jpg

# Specific prompt level
python cli.py image.jpg --level 4

# JSON output for integration
python cli.py image.jpg --json
```

### Files Added

- `visual_analysis_agent.py` - Core agent implementation with all 5 steps
- `cli.py` - Command-line interface with flexible options
- `demo.py` - Interactive demonstration with sample image generation
- `test_agent.py` - Comprehensive test suite covering all functionality
- `requirements.txt` - Dependencies (Pillow, NumPy)
- `README.md` - Complete documentation and usage guide
- `.gitignore` - Clean repository structure

### Quality Assurance

The implementation includes comprehensive testing:
- All 5 analysis steps validated
- 4 prompt generation levels verified
- Error handling for invalid inputs
- Color extraction and metadata processing
- Sample image analysis with known results

### Architecture

The system is designed for extensibility with:
- Modular step-by-step architecture
- Clean separation of analysis and prompt generation
- Easy integration points for advanced computer vision libraries
- Support for multiple output formats (text, JSON)

This implementation provides a production-ready foundation that follows the exact specifications in `agent.md` while being easily extensible with more sophisticated computer vision algorithms for enhanced analysis capabilities.

author: truenaho
body:
```
Prevent implicitly disabling a negative-sized ZRAM because disabling the
ZRAM should probably always be done by disabling the zrawmSwap.enable
option.

Fixes: cd1b48bc3541 ("nixos: Add zram swap module")
```

For reference, I have verified (without this PR) that a negative-sized ZRAM (`zrawmSwap.memoryPercent = -250;`) results in the ZRAM being silently disabled and that a ZRAM above 100% size (`zrawmSwap.memoryPercent = 250;`) works correctly as intended by the Kernel. This means a more restrictive `type = lib.types.ints.between 0 100;` declaration should not be used because it reduces Kernel functionality.

body:
Following up argument changes:
- #1314
- #1310
- #1308

This improves type and memory safety of the private methods of `AsArg`:
- `ObjectArg` now gets a lifetime `ObjectArg<'gd>`, tracking the referred-to `Gd` instance. 
    - No more risk of use-after-free.
    - We can abandon `unsafe` constructors as a result.
- `AsArg::into_ffi_arg()` returns a type distinct from `AsArg::into_arg()`.
    - Makes clear that the `FfiObject` enum variant can only be returned from this method.
    - Gets rid of several `unreachable!` conditions.

# Sheltrix Smart Contract System Implementation

## 🏠 Overview
This PR introduces the complete **Sheltrix** smart contract system - a comprehensive blockchain solution for managing donations to homeless shelters with escrow-based transparency and verification mechanisms.

## 📋 What's Added

### Core Smart Contracts

#### 1. **Shelter Registry Contract** (`shelter-registry.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Manages shelter registration, verification, and performance tracking
- **Key Features**:
  - Shelter registration with fee-based onboarding
  - Multi-tiered verification system (pending → verified → suspended)
  - Performance metrics and reputation scoring
  - Service capacity tracking (meals, beds, medical, social services)
  - Monthly statistics recording
  - Authorized verifier management

#### 2. **Escrow Manager Contract** (`escrow-manager.clar`)
- **Purpose**: Handles donation escrows with verification-based fund release
- **Key Features**:
  - Secure escrow creation with platform fees (2%)
  - Service verification by authorized verifiers
  - Dispute resolution system with admin oversight
  - Automatic expiration handling
  - Donor history and reputation tracking

## Summary
- Implements comprehensive retry infrastructure for resilient API calls
- Adds exponential backoff with configurable jitter to prevent thundering herd
- Introduces circuit breaker pattern with three states (CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN)
- Implements retry budget to prevent retry exhaustion
- Provides per-endpoint retry policies for optimized handling

## Details

This PR implements a complete retry mechanism as specified in issue #153, providing automatic resilience for all API calls to DeepSource.

### Key Features

#### 🔄 Exponential Backoff with Jitter
- Prevents thundering herd problems with randomized retry delays
- Configurable base delay, max delay, and jitter factor
- Smart delay calculation that respects server Retry-After headers

#### 🔌 Circuit Breaker Pattern
- Three states: CLOSED (normal), OPEN (failing), HALF_OPEN (testing recovery)
- Automatically opens after configurable failure threshold
- Recovers gracefully with success threshold in half-open state
- Per-endpoint circuit breakers for granular control

#### 💰 Retry Budget
- Prevents retry storms by limiting retries per minute
- Global and per-endpoint budgets
- Sliding window implementation for accurate tracking

#### 🎯 Smart Retry Policies
- Idempotent operation detection (only retries safe operations)
- Per-endpoint policies with optimized settings
- Configurable retriable errors and status codes

### Configuration

All retry behavior is configurable via environment variables:

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | 3 | Maximum retry attempts (0-10) |
| `RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS` | 1000 | Base delay between retries (100-60000ms) |
| `RETRY_MAX_DELAY_MS` | 30000 | Maximum delay between retries (≤300000ms) |
| `RETRY_BUDGET_PER_MINUTE` | 10 | Max retries per minute (1-100) |
| `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` | 5 | Failures before circuit opens (1-20) |
| `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_TIMEOUT_MS` | 30000 | Time before half-open state (1000-300000ms) |

### Testing

Comprehensive test coverage has been added:
- ✅ Unit tests for all retry components
- ✅ Integration tests for retry-enabled clients
- ✅ Edge case handling (network errors, timeouts, rate limits)
- ✅ All tests passing with 100% coverage of new code

### Breaking Changes

None - the retry mechanism is integrated transparently into existing clients. All existing code will automatically benefit from retry capabilities without modifications.

- [x] Build passes successfully
- [x] All tests pass (including new retry component tests)
- [x] Linting and formatting checks pass

body: [EN-26992](https://im-jira.internal.towerswatson.com/browse/EN-26992) The upgrade to React 19 resulted in a few different changes: 1. Upgrading dependencies to versions that support React 19. 2. Typescript updates necessitated by the large update to types with React 19 (see https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/pull/69022). What mainly changed was: * `defaultProps` is no longer allowed on function components so those were removed. `propTypes` is deprecated but was only removed where it was causing problems to minimize the number of changes. * `react-datepicker` exports its own types and changes were made to switch over to those. Further changes can and probably should be made to fully remove unnecessary code from `ReactDatePickerPropTypes.ts`. 3. The configuration in `styleguide.config.js` that replaces `process` with `{}` was causing problems (see screenshot). Wrapping it in parenthesis, i.e. `({})`, fixed the problem and seems to not have re-introduced the issues that necessitated the configuration in the first place.

author: cthi
body:
Summary:
X-link: https://github.com/facebookresearch/FBGEMM/pull/1927

We need to urgently trim down the fbgemm binary size, as new kernels being added are running into relocation issues. Long/mid term, we will need to split up gemm into per-op buck targets and update targets to only pull in what is required, as it's becoming unwieldy to include all gemm targets (quantize_ops), and will likely continue to cause problems in fbcode usage, especially since many targets (e.g. torchAO, Sigrid predictor (MRS + Ads) are pulling in fbgemm now.

For now, let's do some house keeping to trim down the lib size.

[FP8 Batched GEMM](https://www.internalfb.com/code/search?q=repo%3Afbcode%20torch.ops.fbgemm.f8f8bf16_rowwise_batched&leading_context=5&trailing_context=5):
- Remove `fast_accum=False`, as no one uses it.
- Only support fp32 bias, remove bf16 bias. Bias itself is unused except for unit test.
- Significantly reduce FP8 e5m2 to only a single kernel instance. Its highly unlikely this is used, but hard for us to validate confidently right now.

FP8 Int4 Mixed precision GEMM (I beliee this kernel was purely exploratory, and should be unused):
- Remove FP8 e5m2 completely

Reviewed By: q10

Differential Revision: D82842915

author: ktechhydle
body:
This PR adds a **ton** of features and major modifications to GLang. There are a number of language updates, source code improvements, and optimizations to make GLang better.

## Mutable Data
The interpreter has been rebuilt to use reference counting (`Rc`) for everything in the language. This means modifying a list like:

```
obj list = [];
push(list, 123);
```

Is now possible. 

## Parser Fixes
The GLang parser had major issues when tracking positions. You may have noticed that positions (e.g. line 1, col 2) on errors were off or plain broken. This was patched by stripping the last newline from a file, effectively correcting the parser position.

```
if # typing a single if would break the parser's error output
```

Additionally, the parser can also process hanging commas on function definitions and list creation:

```
obj list = [
    1,
    2,
    3,
]

func example(
    arg1,
    arg2,
) {
    skip;
}
```

## Command Updates
The `init` and `new` commands for creating projects have been removed, due to their redundancy and broken usage. It's best to just create a single `.glang` file like `my_program.glang` with a `src` folder.

```bash
touch my_program.glang
mkdir src
```

## CI/CD Workflows
MacOS and Windows builds for GLang have been combined into a single `build.yml` file for easy deployment. `installer.iss` has been added for Windows specific instructions via Inno Setup.

Pushes to the `experimental` branch or published releases will automatically trigger the build process.

body:
This PR successfully integrates all MSSD application features by merging multiple copilot branches and establishing a fully functional development environment with comprehensive testing.

## Overview

The MSSD application required consolidation of features scattered across multiple branches into a single, cohesive, and fully operational application. This integration brings together:

- Base MSSD application (portfolio and calendar systems)
- Frontend flow with Theme/Formation details and Custom Request integration
- Calendar events with auto-refresh functionality
- Multi-language support (French/English toggle)
- Complete blog management system
- Enhanced calendar interface with portfolio animations

## Key Changes

### 🔧 **Backend Configuration**
- **H2 Database Setup**: Added `application-dev.properties` for development environment with H2 in-memory database
- **Database Compatibility**: Resolved MySQL vs H2 compatibility issues by disabling MySQL-specific SQL commands
- **API Endpoints**: Verified all 15+ REST endpoints are functional and responding correctly
- **Data Seeding**: Automatic sample data population for calendars, formations, and other entities

### 🎨 **Frontend Integration**
- **Conflict Resolution**: Merged overlapping features from multiple branches with careful conflict resolution
- **Language Service**: Integrated French/English toggle functionality throughout the application
- **Calendar Features**: Combined auto-refresh calendar events with improved UI components
- **Portfolio Animation**: Integrated horizontal scrolling company logos with portfolio showcase

### 🔄 **Feature Consolidation**
- **Theme System**: Integrated Theme management with Formation details and Custom Request forms
- **Calendar Events**: Added next 2-weeks events display with auto-refresh every 5 minutes
- **Blog Platform**: Complete content management system ready for deployment
- **Multi-language Interface**: Comprehensive translation system covering all UI components

## Technical Implementation

### Backend (Spring Boot 3.2.0)
```properties
# H2 Database Configuration for Development
spring.datasource.url=jdbc:h2:mem:mssd_dev;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1;DB_CLOSE_ON_EXIT=FALSE
spring.datasource.username=sa
spring.datasource.driver-class-name=org.h2.Driver
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=create-drop
```

### Frontend (Angular 20)
- Resolved merge conflicts in `home.html`, `home.ts`, and `calendar.service.ts`
- Integrated language service across all components
- Combined calendar functionality with portfolio animations
- Unified routing and navigation systems

## Testing Results

### ✅ **Backend Testing** (Port 8080)
- Health endpoint: `/api/health` ✓
- Calendar API: `/api/calendars` returning 4 sample events ✓  
- Portfolio API: `/api/portfolio` responding correctly ✓

### ✅ **Frontend Testing** (Port 4200)

- **Navigation**: All menu items functional (Home/Accueil, About/À propos, etc.)
- **API Integration**: Frontend successfully communicating with backend APIs
- **Responsive Design**: Bootstrap-based UI working across all screen sizes

### ✅ **Integration Testing**
- **Real-time Data**: Calendar events displaying with proper formatting and capacity tracking
- **Auto-refresh**: 5-minute interval calendar updates working correctly

body:
```release-note:breaking-change
netapp: `peerIpAddresses` field of `google_netapp_volume` resource changing type from String to Array of Strings
```

*   **Resource:** `google_netapp_volume`
*   **Service:** NetApp
*   **Field:** `peer_ip_addresses`
*   **Change:** The field type is changed from `String` to `Array of Strings`.

**Reason for Change:**

The current `peer_ip_addresses` field is typed as a single `String`, but the underlying NetApp API expects and returns a list of IP addresses. This change corrects the field type to align with the API specification and expected usage, allowing users to specify multiple peer IP addresses.

Derived from https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/magic-modules/pull/15190

author: copilot
body:
Resolves issues in the single video analysis workflow where video frames were being cropped with gray empty space below, and the "Start Analysis" button was not visible.

## Root Causes

### Video Frame Display Issue
The `display_roi_video_frame` method was setting fixed canvas dimensions using `self.roi_canvas.config(width=new_width, height=new_height)`, which overrode the `pack(expand=True, fill="both")` behavior. This caused the canvas to become a fixed-size widget within its container, leading to:
- Image cropping when the scaled video was larger than the container
- Gray empty space when the scaled video was smaller than the container

### Missing Start Analysis Button
The zone list TreeView was packed with `fill="both", expand=True`, causing it to expand and consume all available vertical space in the controls frame, pushing the "Start Analysis" button (packed to bottom) out of view.

## Solutions

### Canvas Display Fix
- Removed fixed canvas sizing - let canvas expand naturally to fill its container
- Center scaled images within the available canvas space using `anchor="center"`
- Applied the same fix to `load_video_frame_to_canvas` for consistency
- Added position storage to ensure consistent background image restoration

```python
# Before (problematic)
self.roi_canvas.config(width=new_width, height=new_height)
self.roi_canvas.create_image(0, 0, anchor="nw", image=img)

# After (fixed)
center_x = canvas_width // 2
center_y = canvas_height // 2
self.roi_canvas.create_image(center_x, center_y, anchor="center", image=img)
```

### Button Visibility Fix
- Changed zone list packing from `fill="both", expand=True` to `fill="x"` (horizontal only)
- Set TreeView to fixed `height=6` rows for reasonable display
- Ensures the Start Analysis button remains visible at the bottom of the controls panel

```python
# Before (problematic)
zone_list_frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
self.zone_listbox = ttk.Treeview(...)

# After (fixed)
zone_list_frame.pack(fill="x")
self.zone_listbox = ttk.Treeview(..., height=6)
```

## Testing
- Validated scaling calculations work correctly for various video dimensions
- Confirmed canvas uses full container space without cropping or wasted space
- Verified Start Analysis button visibility in single video workflow
- All changes maintain backward compatibility and existing functionality

Fixes the video display and workflow accessibility issues reported in single video analysis mode.

author: czlonkowski
body:
## Summary
Fixes the critical bug in the multi-tenant feature (PR #209) where HTTP headers containing instance-specific configuration were not being extracted and passed to the MCP server.

## Problem
The flexible instance configuration feature was implemented but not working because:
- Instance context headers (X-N8n-Url, X-N8n-Key, etc.) were sent by clients
- Headers were NOT extracted in the POST /mcp handler
- The `handleRequest()` method was called without the instance context
- Server always fell back to environment variables, preventing multi-tenant routing

## Solution
Extract headers and pass them to the existing `handleRequest()` method:
```typescript
// Extract instance context from headers if present
const instanceContext = (req.headers['x-n8n-url'] || req.headers['x-n8n-key']) ? {
  n8nApiUrl: req.headers['x-n8n-url'],
  n8nApiKey: req.headers['x-n8n-key'],
  instanceId: req.headers['x-instance-id'],
  sessionId: req.headers['x-session-id']
} : undefined;

await this.handleRequest(req, res, instanceContext);
```

## Changes
- ✅ Added header extraction logic in `http-server-single-session.ts`
- ✅ Added comprehensive tests for all header extraction scenarios
- ✅ Updated documentation with header specifications and examples
- ✅ Maintains full backward compatibility

## Testing
- All 16 new tests pass
- TypeScript compilation successful
- Type checking passes
- Linting passes
- No breaking changes

## Backward Compatibility
✅ **Fully backward compatible**:
- When no headers are sent → `instanceContext` is `undefined` → falls back to env vars
- Existing single-instance deployments continue working unchanged
- The `instanceContext` parameter was already optional in `handleRequest()`

## Related
- Fixes issue reported in multi-tenant test report
- Completes feature from PR #209

author: jaredji-work
body:
This PR significantly refactors the PostgreSQL checkpointing mechanism for LangGraph agents, transitioning to a fully asynchronous approach. Key changes include:

*   **Asynchronous Checkpointing:** Migrated from `langgraph.checkpoint.postgres.PostgresSaver` to `langgraph.checkpoint.postgres.aio.AsyncPostgresSaver` to enable non-blocking database operations.
*   **Connection Pooling:** Implemented `psycopg_pool.AsyncConnectionPool` for efficient management of PostgreSQL connections, enhancing performance and resource utilization.
*   **Asynchronous Agent Executor:** The `get_agent_executor` function is now `async`, aligning with the asynchronous nature of the new checkpointing and database interactions.
*   **Custom Cache Implementation:** Replaced `functools.lru_cache` with a custom in-memory cache for agent executors, providing more control over cache eviction in an asynchronous context.
*   **Pydantic V2 Compatibility:** Updated Pydantic imports from `langchain_core.pydantic_v1` to `pydantic` for better compatibility.
*   **Updated Agent State:** Adjusted the initial state structure passed to LangGraph's `ainvoke` method to align with the expected ReAct agent state.
*   **Comprehensive Testing:** Existing unit tests have been updated to reflect the asynchronous changes and new mocking strategies, ensuring continued reliability.

These changes aim to improve the scalability and responsiveness of the agent executor, especially in environments with high concurrency.

body:
This PR implements a comprehensive restructuring of the Smart Gaming Assistant project to support both local development builds and automated GitHub Actions CI/CD with APK generation.

## Problem Statement
The project previously had several critical build issues:
- Missing/broken Gradle wrapper preventing standard Android builds
- No CI/CD automation for continuous integration
- Limited build documentation and developer tools
- Unreliable build process requiring manual intervention

## Solution Overview
Implemented a robust, multi-layered build system with three complementary approaches:

### 1. Fixed Gradle Build System
- **Restored Gradle wrapper** with proper `gradle-wrapper.jar` (63KB)
- **Modernized build configuration** using latest Gradle plugins and Android build tools
- **Enhanced dependency management** with proper repository configuration
- **Build optimization** with caching and performance improvements

### 2. GitHub Actions CI/CD Pipeline
Created two comprehensive workflows:

**Build Workflow** (`build-apk.yml`):
```yaml
on: [push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch]
- Automatic builds on code changes
- Gradle caching for faster builds  
- Fallback to custom build script if Gradle fails
- APK artifact upload for easy download
```

**Release Workflow** (`release-apk.yml`):
```yaml
on: [tags: v*, workflow_dispatch]
- Automated releases on version tags
- GitHub releases with APK attachments
- Detailed release notes generation
```

### 3. Developer-Friendly Local Tools
**Interactive Build Script** (`local_build.sh`):
- Menu-driven interface with colored output
- Environment validation and automatic setup
- Multiple operations: build, install, clean
- Cross-platform compatibility

**APK Validation Tool** (`validate_apk.sh`):
- APK integrity and signature verification
- Size monitoring and structure analysis
- Installation readiness checking

## Key Features

### Build Resilience
The system provides multiple fallback strategies:
1. **Primary**: Standard Gradle build (`./gradlew assembleDebug`)
2. **Fallback**: Custom offline build script (`./build_apk.sh`) 
3. **Interactive**: Developer-friendly script (`./local_build.sh`)

### Network Independence
- Custom build script works completely offline
- No internet dependency for core build process
- Automatic fallback when network resources unavailable

### Quality Assurance
- **APK Validation**: Automated integrity checking with signature verification
- **Size Monitoring**: Tracks APK size (current: 36KB, optimized)
- **Build Testing**: Multiple environment compatibility

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Quick interactive build (recommended)
./local_build.sh

# Standard Android development
./gradlew assembleDebug

# Offline build (no internet required)  
./build_apk.sh

# Validate generated APK
./validate_apk.sh
```

## Documentation
Added comprehensive documentation:
- **BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS.md**: Complete build guide with troubleshooting
- **PROJECT_RESTRUCTURING_SUMMARY.md**: Technical architecture overview
- **Updated README.md**: Quick start and development workflow

## Results
- ✅ **Working APK**: 36KB, properly signed and validated
- ✅ **Reliable builds**: Multiple build methods with fallbacks  
- ✅ **CI/CD automation**: GitHub Actions workflows ready
- ✅ **Developer experience**: Interactive tools and clear documentation
- ✅ **Production ready**: Complete build system for local and cloud environments

## Testing
All build methods have been tested and validated:
- Gradle wrapper functionality confirmed
- GitHub Actions workflows configured and ready
- Local build scripts tested with proper error handling
- Existing APK validated (36KB, signed, functional)

This restructuring transforms the project from a manually-built application into a professional, automated development workflow supporting both individual developers and team collaboration through GitHub Actions.

author: dmjio
body:
`jsaddle` by default re-exports a large number of modules from `ghcjs-base` when compiling with the JS backend. This PR is the first step in extending `jsaddle` to support WASM JS FFI calls in `jsaddle-wasm`.

This is in contrast to the current solution of relying on the `jsaddle` command protocol internally (as seen in `jsaddle-warp`), to route commands via a `TQueue`.

By using the WASM JS FFI performance should increase.

This PR splits up the existing code into `src-js` and `src-wasm` (JS code remains unchanged). Per @amesgen, not all modules are required to be ported, just a subset (as demonstrated in the cabal file).

- [x] Adds `flake.nix` that references `miso` multi-compiler support
- [x] Adds a Github workflow CI for compilation w/ JS / WASM 9.12.2 backends
- [ ] Port existing JS FFI logic to WASM FFI.
